subject: 🏃 Tuesday — 4×1 mi Threshold on the Esplanade (Wk 5)
html:
Tomorrow: 4×1 mi threshold on the Charles River Esplanade — the first quality session of Phase 2. No track in Boston, so we run it on flat river path. 1 mi easy jog from the hotel over the footbridge to the river, then 4×1 mi threshold with 90s walk/jog recovery between reps, then 1 mi easy back. ~7 mi total. Use the BU Bridge ↔ Mass Ave Bridge stretch (~1 mi flat straight) so you're not fighting bridge crossings mid-rep. Pre-run activation (5 min in the room first): quadruped hip CARs (3 each direction, each leg — sink into the IR at the bottom), banded lateral walks (10 each direction), glute bridges (10, 2-sec hold), and the PT-prescribed quadruped banded hip IR (5–10 each side) — pack the resistance band tonight.

HR is the anchor, pace is the check. Hold each rep at 155–165 BPM, hard cap 165 — target pace 7:15–7:25 but accept whatever your legs give at the correct HR. This is jet-lag day 2: at 6 AM ET your body clock reads 3 AM PT, so the legs will be a step slow and that's expected. A 7:35 mile at HR 162 is a complete threshold dose — do NOT chase 7:15 on a 3-AM-body-clock morning. Pace short of prescription at correct HR is information about today's freshness, not a failed workout.

Cold gate — neck-check at the alarm. This is your first hard effort since the PAL 10K while sick (7:17/mi, HR capped 166). You're day 7–8 and trending right — yesterday's recovery run was clean (HR 134, zero seconds above Z2). If symptoms are above-the-neck and clearly improving, run it as written. Any chest involvement, productive cough, or resting HR still elevated → convert to 5–6 mi easy on the Esplanade and we bank the threshold for Thursday's progression. No heroics on a cold tail.

Focus cue: cap every rep at 165 and let pace float. The engine's already calibrated — May 26's 6×1000m confirmed VDOT 54–55 — so tomorrow's job is the threshold dose, not a pace PR. Context: Week 5 of 12, Phase 2 (Strength & Threshold) opens — 54 days to the SF Marathon. Knee's been 1/5 across all of Phase 1; keep logging it. Tonight: lights out by 10 PM ET to keep defusing the eastbound jet lag, lay out run kit + the band, and set the alarm with enough buffer for the warm-up jog to the river.
